name: Off-by-one Error
principle: The code calculates or uses a maximum or minimum value that is exactly 1 too high or 1 too low. This can make loops, allocations, indexes, or string length arguments cross a boundary by one element or byte.
detection_signals: for/while loop uses i <= SIZE with access arr[i]
array access arr[SIZE] after allocation or declaration of SIZE elements
malloc(n * sizeof(T)) followed by writing sentinel list[n] = NULL
character buffer size equals maximum text length without +1 for '\0'
strncat(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) or strncat(dst, src, remaining) without -1
sprintf(dst, ...) maximum formatted text length equals sizeof(dst)
Java loop uses i <= array.length with array[i]
negative_signals: loop condition is i < SIZE for zero-based array access
allocation includes sentinel or terminator space: malloc((n + 1) * sizeof(T))
strncat length argument is sizeof(dst) - strlen(dst) - 1
snprintf(dst, sizeof(dst), ...) is used and return value is checked for truncation
index is checked as index >= 0 && index < array.length before access
false_defense_traps: Using strncat with sizeof(dst) as the third argument; it is the max characters to append, not total destination size.
Using <= because the upper bound looks inclusive; valid zero-based indexes end at SIZE - 1.
Allocating exactly n elements and then writing a NULL or sentinel at element n.
Counting visible formatted characters but not the automatic trailing NUL.
Assuming a one-byte overflow is harmless.
verification_focus: Does any boundary, length, allocation, or index calculation differ from the correct limit by exactly one, especially for terminators or sentinels?

consequence_chains.trigger: allocation omits one terminator or sentinel slot and code writes it
consequence_chains.consequence: one-past-end write, memory corruption, crash, or code execution

consequence_chains.trigger: string length calculation leaves no space for the trailing NUL
consequence_chains.consequence: improper null termination and later out-of-bounds string processing

consequence_chains.trigger: loop bound permits index SIZE for an array with valid indexes 0..SIZE-1
consequence_chains.consequence: operation outside buffer bounds and possible data corruption

consequence_chains.trigger: off-by-one boundary value reaches an assertion-protected impossible state
consequence_chains.consequence: reachable assertion and denial of service

patch_principle: Use half-open bounds for zero-based arrays: 0 <= i && i < size.
Include space for NUL terminators and sentinel elements in allocation and validation.
Pass remaining capacity minus one to C string append/copy APIs that add a terminator.
Prefer bounded formatting APIs such as snprintf and validate truncation.
Test boundary inputs at size-1, size, and size+1.

minimal_examples.vuln: for (i = 0; i <= PATH_SIZE; i++) filename[i] = c;
minimal_examples.safe: for (i = 0; i < PATH_SIZE; i++) filename[i] = c;
